name: Aneurysmal Bone Cyst

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiologic and histopathologic criteria for aneurysmal bone cyst

criteria.description: Expansile, lytic bone lesion with characteristic fluid-fluid levels on MRI or CT
Histology showing blood-filled cystic spaces separated by fibrous septa containing osteoclast-type giant cells
Localized pain and swelling at the affected bone site

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic radiologic features plus confirmatory histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other cystic or neoplastic bone lesions.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Expansile osteolytic bone lesion with fluid-fluid levels
pathognomonic.notes: Identified on MRI or CT imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Blood-filled cystic spaces within bone lesion

common.symptomName: Swelling or palpable mass over affected bone
Reduced range of motion if lesion near joint

occasional.symptomName: Tenderness on palpation of affected area

searchTerms: increased temperature on skin over lesion

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to nerve compression
occasional.notes: If lesion is adjacent to neural structures

searchTerms: back pain with nerve compression signs
weakness or numbness from spinal cord squeezing

rare.symptomName: Soft tissue extension beyond bone cortex
searchTerms: extension of lesion into surrounding tissue

laboratory: Typically normal laboratory studies; no specific biomarkers
imaging: Expansile lytic bone lesion with thin sclerotic margins
Characteristic fluid-fluid levels on MRI or CT
genetic: USP6 gene rearrangements in primary aneurysmal bone cysts
other: Histopathology showing blood-filled cystic spaces separated by fibrous septa with osteoclast-type giant cells

distinguishingFeatures: Typically occurs in skeletally mature adults
Lacks characteristic fluid-fluid levels on imaging
Histology shows mononuclear stromal cells with multinucleated giant cells but no blood-filled cystic spaces
Malignant tumor with aggressive radiologic features
Presence of malignant osteoid on histology

redFlags: Neurological deficits indicating spinal cord or nerve compression
Pathologic fracture with significant bone destruction
references: Dorfman HD, Czerniak B. Bone Cancers. Cancer. 1995;75(1 Suppl):203-210.
Kransdorf MJ, Sweet DE. Aneurysmal bone cyst: concept, controversy, clinical presentation, and imaging. AJR Am J Roentgenol. 1995;164(3):573-580.
Oliveira AM, Hsi BL, Weremowicz S, et al. USP6 (Tre2) fusion oncogenes in aneurysmal bone cyst. Cancer Res. 2004;64(6):1920-1923.
